rendered: The review starts from the known global cobalt reserves, given as ≈7 million[1] in total, taken from the USGS report on cobalt published in 2021[2]. It then applies a conservative mining efficiency of ≈70%[3] per year, and assumes that ≈40%[4] of the mined cobalt is directed toward battery manufacturing. The review's recomputation chains these inputs (total reserves, mining efficiency, battery share), and the total usable battery-specific cobalt from the reserves falls to ≈2 million[5] metric tons globally. The review presents this as its own recomputed estimate, and the document does not show the intermediate product of these factors. This reduced figure is what the review contrasts with projected demand, which it says would exceed available reserves before 2045[6] unless Co-free cathodes or recycling are implemented.
